Checked-fix corpus. Read by scripts/evaluate-fixes.py; not collected by pytest.

Each case is a working module. `break`/`to` is a mutation applied to it (exact text, once; `\n`
is a newline) that produces the problem a model is asked to fix. The check after `--- check ---`
runs against the module and must pass for the working code and fail for the broken code, so it
separates the intended fix from one that merely satisfies the type checker. The check is never
shown to the model or to the checker.

Written by hand, 2026-09-14, to cover the diagnostic classes basedpyright reports most in
day-to-day Python -- not collected from use.

=== split-separator · argument-type
break: line.split(",")
   to: line.split(3)
---
def fields(line: str) -> list[str]:
    """One CSV record, split into its comma-separated fields."""
    return line.split(",")


def header(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """The column names: the fields of the first record."""
    return fields(text.splitlines()[0])
--- check ---
assert fields("a,b,c") == ["a", "b", "c"]
assert header("x,y\n1,2") == ["x", "y"]

=== round-places · argument-type
break: round(amount, 2)
   to: round(amount, "2")
---
def price_label(amount: float, currency: str = "EUR") -> str:
    """A price for display, rounded to cents."""
    return f"{round(amount, 2)} {currency}"
--- check ---
assert price_label(3.14159) == "3.14 EUR"

=== parse-count · argument-type
break: count = int(raw)
   to: count = raw
---
def indices(raw: str) -> list[int]:
    """Indices 0..n-1 for a count the user typed as text."""
    count = int(raw)
    return list(range(count))
--- check ---
assert indices("3") == [0, 1, 2]

=== join-numbers · argument-type
break: ", ".join(str(n) for n in numbers)
   to: ", ".join(numbers)
---
def listing(numbers: list[int]) -> str:
    """Ticket numbers as one comma-separated line."""
    return ", ".join(str(n) for n in numbers)
--- check ---
assert listing([4, 8, 15]) == "4, 8, 15"

=== byte-order · argument-type
break: int.from_bytes(data, "big")
   to: int.from_bytes(data, 1)
---
def packet_length(header: bytes) -> int:
    """The length field of a packet: the first two header bytes, big-endian."""
    data = header[:2]
    return int.from_bytes(data, "big")
--- check ---
assert packet_length(b"\x01\x00rest") == 256

=== timedelta-days · argument-type
break: timedelta(days=7)
   to: timedelta(days="7")
---
from datetime import date, timedelta


def next_review(last: date) -> date:
    """Reviews happen weekly: the date one week after the last one."""
    return last + timedelta(days=7)
--- check ---
assert next_review(date(2024, 1, 1)) == date(2024, 1, 8)

=== path-join-year · argument-type

   to: os.path.join(root, year, name)
---
import os


def archive_path(root: str, year: int, name: str) -> str:
    """Where a report is archived: <root>/<year>/<name>."""
    return os.path.join(root, str(year), name)
--- check ---
assert archive_path("/srv", 2024, "q1.pdf") == "/srv/2024/q1.pdf"

=== missing-carry · missing-argument
break: return add(a, b, 0)
   to: return add(a, b)
---
def add(a: int, b: int, carry: int) -> int:
    """One column of long addition: two digits and the carry from the column before."""
    return a + b + carry


def first_column(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """The rightmost column, where nothing has been carried in yet."""
    return add(a, b, 0)
--- check ---
assert first_column(4, 5) == 9

=== missing-timeout · missing-argument
break: return fetch(url, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
   to: return fetch(url)
---
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 5.0


def fetch(url: str, timeout: float) -> str:
    return f"GET {url} (timeout {timeout}s)"


def fetch_default(url: str) -> str:
    """Fetch with the project's default timeout."""
    return fetch(url, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
--- check ---
assert fetch_default("/health") == "GET /health (timeout 5.0s)"

=== missing-note · missing-argument
break: account.deposit(amount, "opening balance")
   to: account.deposit(amount)
---
class Account:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.balance = 0
        self.notes: list[str] = []

    def deposit(self, amount: int, note: str) -> None:
        self.balance += amount
        self.notes.append(note)


def open_account(amount: int) -> Account:
    """A new account holding its opening deposit."""
    account = Account()
    account.deposit(amount, "opening balance")
    return account
--- check ---
acct = open_account(10)
assert acct.balance == 10 and len(acct.notes) == 1

=== strptime-format · missing-argument
break: datetime.strptime(text, "%Y-%m-%d")
   to: datetime.strptime(text)
---
from datetime import datetime


def parse_day(text: str) -> datetime:
    """A day written as an ISO date, e.g. '2024-05-01'."""
    return datetime.strptime(text, "%Y-%m-%d")
--- check ---
assert parse_day("2024-05-01") == datetime(2024, 5, 1)

=== method-on-class · missing-argument
break: return Parser().parse(text)
   to: return Parser.parse(text)
---
class Parser:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.separator = "="

    def parse(self, text: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key, _, value = text.partition(self.separator)
        return key.strip(), value.strip()


def setting(text: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    return Parser().parse(text)
--- check ---
assert setting("color = blue") == ("color", "blue")

=== extra-middle · too-many-arguments
break: return display_name(person["first"], person["last"])
   to: return display_name(person["first"], person["middle"], person["last"])
---
def display_name(first: str, last: str) -> str:
    return f"{first} {last}"


def byline(person: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    """Author line for an article: first and last name only."""
    return display_name(person["first"], person["last"])
--- check ---
assert byline({"first": "Ada", "middle": "King", "last": "Lovelace"}) == "Ada Lovelace"

=== keyword-renamed · unknown-keyword
break: ledger.post(amount, note="rent")
   to: ledger.post(amount, memo="rent")
---
class Ledger:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.entries: list[tuple[int, str]] = []

    def post(self, amount: int, note: str) -> None:
        self.entries.append((amount, note))


def pay_rent(ledger: Ledger, amount: int) -> None:
    ledger.post(amount, note="rent")
--- check ---
ledger = Ledger()
pay_rent(ledger, 900)
assert ledger.entries == [(900, "rent")]

=== dataclass-field · unknown-keyword
break: User(name=name, email=email)
   to: User(name=name, mail=email)
---
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class User:
    name: str
    email: str


def register(name: str, email: str) -> User:
    return User(name=name, email=email)
--- check ---
assert register("ada", "ada@example.org").email == "ada@example.org"

=== splitlines-keepends · unknown-keyword

   to: text.splitlines(keep_ends=True)

def raw_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:

--- check ---

=== regex-no-match · optional-member-access
break: if match is None:\n        return ""\n    return
   to: return
---
import re


def version(tag: str) -> str:
    """The x.y.z version inside a release tag like 'v1.2.3', or '' when there is none."""
    match = re.match(r"v(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", tag)
    if match is None:
        return ""
    return match.group(1)
--- check ---
assert version("v1.2.3") == "1.2.3"
assert version("nightly") == ""

=== next-default · optional-member-access
break: first.upper() if first else ""
   to: first.upper()
---
def shout_first(words: list[str], prefix: str) -> str:
    """The first word starting with prefix, upper-cased; '' when no word does."""
    first = next((w for w in words if w.startswith(prefix)), None)
    return first.upper() if first else ""
--- check ---
assert shout_first(["apple", "avocado"], "av") == "AVOCADO"
assert shout_first([], "x") == ""

=== xml-find · optional-member-access
break: if title is None or title.text is None:\n        return "untitled"\n    return
   to: return
---
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET


def feed_title(xml: str) -> str:
    """The feed's <title>, or 'untitled' when it has none."""
    root = ET.fromstring(xml)
    title = root.find("title")
    if title is None or title.text is None:
        return "untitled"
    return title.text
--- check ---
assert feed_title("<feed><title>News</title></feed>") == "News"
assert feed_title("<feed/>") == "untitled"

=== dict-get-default · optional-operand
break: ages.get(name, 0)
   to: ages.get(name)
---
def age_next_year(ages: dict[str, int], name: str) -> int:
    """Next year's age; someone not in the register is treated as a newborn (age 0 now)."""
    return ages.get(name, 0) + 1
--- check ---
assert age_next_year({"ada": 36}, "ada") == 37
assert age_next_year({}, "bob") == 1

=== optional-greeting · optional-operand
break: (name or "world")
   to: name
---
def greeting(name: str | None = None) -> str:
    """'Hello, <name>', or 'Hello, world' when nobody is named."""
    return "Hello, " + (name or "world")
--- check ---
assert greeting("Ada") == "Hello, Ada"
assert greeting() == "Hello, world"

=== import-path · undefined-name
break: from pathlib import Path\n
   to:
---
from pathlib import Path


def extension(filename: str) -> str:
    """The file extension without the dot: 'archive.tar.gz' reports 'gz'."""
    return Path(filename).suffix.lstrip(".")
--- check ---
assert extension("archive.tar.gz") == "gz"

=== import-defaultdict · undefined-name
break: from collections import defaultdict\n
   to:
---
from collections import defaultdict


def by_initial(names: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Names grouped under their first letter."""
    groups: defaultdict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for name in names:
        groups[name[0]].append(name)
    return dict(groups)
--- check ---
assert by_initial(["ada", "alan", "bob"]) == {"a": ["ada", "alan"], "b": ["bob"]}

=== import-field · undefined-name
break: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
   to: from dataclasses import dataclass
---
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Cart:
    items: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def add(self, item: str) -> None:
        self.items.append(item)
--- check ---
a, b = Cart(), Cart()
a.add("tea")
assert b.items == []

=== typo-total · undefined-name
break: return total
   to: return totl
---
def invoice_total(lines: list[tuple[str, float]]) -> float:
    """Sum of the line amounts on an invoice."""
    total = 0.0
    for _, amount in lines:
        total += amount
    return total
--- check ---
assert invoice_total([("tea", 2.5), ("cake", 3.0)]) == 5.5

=== renamed-helper · undefined-name
break: return [_normalise(tag) for tag in tags]
   to: return [_normalize(tag) for tag in tags]
---
def _normalise(tag: str) -> str:
    return tag.strip().lower()


def clean_tags(tags: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Tags trimmed and lower-cased."""
    return [_normalise(tag) for tag in tags]
--- check ---
assert clean_tags([" Python ", "NEOVIM"]) == ["python", "neovim"]

=== startswith-typo · attribute
break: line.startswith("#")
   to: line.startwith("#")
---
def code_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Lines of a config file that are not comments (comments start with '#')."""
    return [line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith("#")]
--- check ---
assert code_lines("# note\nx = 1") == ["x = 1"]

=== list-push · attribute
break: stack.append(token)
   to: stack.push(token)
---
def reverse_tokens(tokens: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Tokens in reverse order, using an explicit stack."""
    stack: list[str] = []
    for token in tokens:
        stack.append(token)
    return [stack.pop() for _ in range(len(stack))]
--- check ---
assert reverse_tokens(["a", "b", "c"]) == ["c", "b", "a"]

=== dict-iteritems · attribute
break: prices.items()
   to: prices.iteritems()
---
def cheap(prices: dict[str, float], limit: float) -> list[str]:
    """Names of products that cost less than limit."""
    return [name for name, price in prices.items() if price < limit]
--- check ---
assert cheap({"tea": 2.0, "wine": 12.0}, 5.0) == ["tea"]

=== enum-member-typo · attribute
break: Light.GREEN if
   to: Light.GREN if
---
from enum import Enum


class Light(Enum):
    RED = "red"
    AMBER = "amber"
    GREEN = "green"


def after(light: Light) -> Light:
    """The next light in the cycle red -> green -> amber -> red."""
    return Light.GREEN if light is Light.RED else Light.AMBER if light is Light.GREEN else Light.RED
--- check ---
assert after(Light.RED) is Light.GREEN
assert after(Light.GREEN) is Light.AMBER
assert after(Light.AMBER) is Light.RED

=== self-attribute-typo · attribute
break: return self.balance >= amount
   to: return self.balence >= amount
---
class Wallet:
    def __init__(self, balance: int) -> None:
        self.balance = balance

    def can_afford(self, amount: int) -> bool:
        return self.balance >= amount
--- check ---
assert Wallet(10).can_afford(5)
assert not Wallet(1).can_afford(5)

=== missing-await · async
break: body = await fetch_body(url)
   to: body = fetch_body(url)
---
import asyncio


async def fetch_body(url: str) -> str:
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    return f"<html>{url}</html>"


async def title_of(url: str) -> str:
    body = await fetch_body(url)
    return body.removeprefix("<html>").removesuffix("</html>")
--- check ---
assert asyncio.run(title_of("home")) == "home"

=== property-called · call
break: return shape.area * count
   to: return shape.area() * count
---
class Square:
    def __init__(self, side: float) -> None:
        self.side = side

    @property
    def area(self) -> float:
        return self.side * self.side


def tiles_needed(shape: Square, count: int) -> float:
    return shape.area * count
--- check ---
assert tiles_needed(Square(2.0), 3) == 12.0

def word_count(text: str) -> int:

    return len(text.split())
--- check ---

=== returns-optional · return-type

   to: users.get(user_id)
---
def author(users: dict[int, str], user_id: int) -> str:
    """Display name for a comment's author; deleted users show as 'anonymous'."""
    return users.get(user_id, "anonymous")
--- check ---
assert author({1: "ada"}, 1) == "ada"
assert author({}, 2) == "anonymous"

def parity(n: int) -> str:
    """'even' or 'odd'."""
    if n % 2 == 0:
        return "even"
    return "odd"
--- check ---
assert parity(4) == "even"
assert parity(3) == "odd"

=== tuple-unpack · assignment
break: name, _, domain = address.partition("@")
   to: name, domain = address.partition("@")
---
def mail_domain(address: str) -> str:
    """The part of an e-mail address after the '@'."""
    name, _, domain = address.partition("@")
    return domain if name else ""
--- check ---
assert mail_domain("ada@example.org") == "example.org"

=== annotated-assignment · assignment
break: timeout: float = float(raw)
   to: timeout: float = raw
---
def parse_timeout(raw: str) -> float:
    """Seconds, from a configuration value such as '2.5'."""
    timeout: float = float(raw)
    return max(timeout, 0.0)
--- check ---
assert parse_timeout("2.5") == 2.5

=== possibly-unbound-else · possibly-unbound
break:     else:\n        letter = "C"\n
   to:
---
def grade(score: int) -> str:
    """A for 90 and up, B for 50 and up, C below that."""
    if score >= 90:
        letter = "A"
    elif score >= 50:
        letter = "B"
    else:
        letter = "C"
    return letter
--- check ---
assert grade(95) == "A"
assert grade(10) == "C"

=== unbound-after-except · possibly-unbound
break: data = {}
   to: pass
---
import json


def load_settings(text: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Parsed settings; malformed JSON counts as no settings at all."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        data = {}
    return data
--- check ---
assert load_settings('{"a": 1}') == {"a": 1}
assert load_settings("{") == {}

=== missing-colon · syntax
break: def is_blank(line: str) -> bool:
   to: def is_blank(line: str) -> bool
---
def is_blank(line: str) -> bool:
    """True for lines holding only whitespace."""
    return not line.strip()


def blank_count(text: str) -> int:
    return sum(1 for line in text.splitlines() if is_blank(line))
--- check ---
assert blank_count("a\n\n  \nb") == 2

=== unclosed-paren · syntax

   to: max(values, key=abs
---
def largest_magnitude(values: list[int]) -> int:
    """The value furthest from zero, keeping its sign."""
    return max(values, key=abs)
--- check ---
assert largest_magnitude([3, -7, 5]) == -7
